# Agile Delivery Knowledge Kit

> Playbooks, decision guides, and templates for predictable delivery on distributed teams.

## Overview

- [Home](./): Field-tested playbooks, decision guides, and templates for distributed engineering teams that want predictable delivery.

## Getting started

- [Observe first](getting-started/observe-first/): How a delivery lead joins a new team by observing, helping, and asking questions before proposing change.

## Playbooks

- [Relative estimation](playbooks/relative-estimation/): Why story points measure size relative to other work, not days, and how to coach a team out of the points-equal-days habit.
- [Capacity planning](playbooks/capacity-planning/): Forecast sprint and quarterly commitments from actual past velocity, adjusted for holidays and time off across locations.
- [Feature Launch Reservations](playbooks/feature-launch-reservations/): Reserve time with the teams you depend on during quarterly planning, instead of scrambling for help mid-quarter.
- [WIP limits and swarming](playbooks/wip-limits-and-swarming/): Limit work in progress and swarm on the highest-priority item to finish work steadily instead of in an end-of-sprint spike.
- [Sprint reviews](playbooks/sprint-reviews/): Run sprint reviews as working sessions where stakeholders see finished work and shape what comes next.

## Decision guides

- [Straight-through approval](decision-guides/straight-through-approval/): Decide when a design built on pre-approved standard components can skip the full review and get a fast approval.
- [Does this launch need a reservation?](decision-guides/does-this-need-a-reservation/): A quick triage to decide whether a launch needs a Feature Launch Reservation or can launch and be monitored asynchronously.

## Templates

- [Reservation request](reusable-templates/reservation-request/): Copy-and-fill template for booking a Feature Launch Reservation with a supporting team.

## Overview

- [Contributing](contributing/): The docs-as-code workflow for this kit, including required front matter and the automated checks every pull request must pass.
- [About](about/): Who built this knowledge kit, why, and how each part maps to modern knowledge operations practice.
